To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a self adaptive high frequency injection (SAdHFI) based sensorless control scheme for IPMSM has been developed.

The proposed self-adaptive HFI based sensorless control scheme is capable of accurately estimating the position and speed of the machine even in presence of saturation and parameter variations, and of providing a very accurate control of the drive.

a novel sensorless drive control strategy is proposed, based on the use of high frequency voltage injection and a self adaptive control scheme, which allows on line tuning of the sensor-less control parameters, and of the current controllers, leading to improved performance and reduced losses.

the following topics: - High frequency injection (HIFI) based position and rotor speed sensorless estimation algorithms for interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSM) and switched reluctance machines (SRM), including a novel self adaptive procedure for the auto tuning and self-adaptation of the HIFI based sensorless control.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method allows for the first time to obtain a sensorless control system with high accuracy, high robustness and low losses, without requiring any a priori information on the machine parameters.
the proposed method can be applied to both IPMSM and SRM drives, and it is a very effective and simple way to improve the accuracy of sensorless control.
the proposed self adaptive high frequency injection method is a very powerful tool for the implementation of a robust sensorless control scheme for IPMSM/SynRM drives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method allows to achieve high accuracy in position estimation, while avoiding any a priori machine parameters knowledge.
the proposed method can be easily applied to any kind of sensorless control strategy, with no need for any a priori machine parameter estimation.
the proposed approach allows for the implementation of a robust and reliable sensorless control strategy for IPMSM/SynRM drives, which can be applied in real industrial applications.
